extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors in public policy, nonprofit management, corporate/NGO communications, and crisis media strategy
extracted.subtask_description: A Harvard Kennedy School teaching case about the Planned Parenthood / Susan G. Komen controversy that asks students to analyze how social and mainstream media shaped organizational decisions, the effects of campaigns, and the costs of inaction in a social-media driven environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a well-managed social media campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: This case explores "the effect of a well-managed social media campaign" — how social media can drive social change and influence organizational outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess campaign reach, message virality, timing, calls-to-action, coordination across platforms, sentiment mobilization, and whether online activism translated into real-world pressure or organizational change (e.g., the flooding of social media messages supporting Planned Parenthood and criticizing Komen). Consider measurable outcomes such as public attention, fundraising impact, and policy reversals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of inaction in a social media–driven environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are asked to consider "the cost of inaction in a social media driven environment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how failure to respond or delayed response can escalate reputational damage, allow narratives to harden, and force reactive decision-making. Use the Komen example (capitulated after four days of social and mass media criticism) to analyze timelines and opportunity costs of different response strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mainstream press and social media to appeal to constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each organization appealed to its constituents—using the mainstream press and social media outlets—to support their position."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how effectively an organization integrates traditional media and social channels: target audiences, message consistency, timing, spokespeople, and amplification strategies. Consider selection of channels for different stakeholder groups and how messages were tailored to supporters versus the broader public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message framing and positioning (mission vs. political framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Komen leaders "emphasized the importance of administering high quality grants to direct service providers; Planned Parenthood claimed that women's health was being jeopardized for the sake of political expediency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how each organization framed the issue (operational/mission-focused vs. political/values-focused), the persuasive appeals used, evidence and narratives presented, and which frames resonated with publics. Consider anti-patterns such as mixed or defensive messaging that can undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis decision-making and policy justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Komen cited "newly adopted criteria barring grants to organizations that are under investigation by local, state or federal authorities" and referenced a congressional investigation as the reason for the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the legitimacy, transparency, and defensibility of internal policy decisions used as public justification. Consider whether the rationale matches communicated values, whether due process and stakeholder consultation occurred, and how citing investigations or legal factors affects public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder mobilization and public engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The controversy "drew politicians, activists, the press and supporters of both organizations into a painful battle" and social media "were flooded with messages largely supporting Planned Parenthood and castigating Komen."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess capacity to mobilize supporters (volume and coordination of messages, use of influencers, calls to action), the speed and scale of engagement, and whether mobilization translated into pressure on decision-makers. Look for tactics that amplify grassroots voice versus astroturfing risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputational impact and trust management
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned Parenthood accused Komen of "bowing to pressure from anti-abortion activists" and described the action as "hurtful," illustrating reputational harm and trust erosion between organizations and constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze short- and long-term impacts on brand reputation, stakeholder trust, donor relationships, and inter-organizational partnerships. Consider strategies for repair, apology, transparency, and rebuilding credibility after perceived capitulation or politicized decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative control and counter-messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: The case highlights competing narratives: Komen's administrative/quality-of-grants narrative versus accusations of political capitulation, with both sides using media to push their story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how and whether organizations maintained control of the dominant narrative, the use of counter-messaging to rebut accusations, speed of corrective communications, and the role of third-party endorsements or investigative framing in shifting public perception.
